Game lacks player agency and doesn't provide enough variety in upgrades. Beating the game isn't as satisfying as I hoped. You can almost always tell what runs have legs early in the run. It feels like a roguelike before you get any meta progression and the game is very simple. I was expecting to unlock entirely new mechanics and levels, but what yo start with appears to be what you get. It's a cool idea, with a lot of potential, but don't expect it to keep you busy for more than an hour or two. I think it needs a bit more time before I can really recommend it for it's current price. I hope in a year or two and a few more updates I can change my review.

7/10 The game is pretty fun while you're learning. I beat all the modes and tried most of the "build" variations you come across. Ultimately, the game is missing a great deal when it comes to "builds." The fundamental strategy for every run, regardless of which paths you take, is exactly the same. It remains true through the entire run. There are small deviations you'll make, depending on path choice, but they don't change anything about your strategy overall. To make a comparison, the game is like running a marathon. The different "build" paths are like wearing different shoes and deciding to wear a hat, or not, while running that marathon. Sure there are some differences, but you're still just running. This issue, for a player like me, makes the game ultimately fall flat. I had some great runs, and even broke the point system in one, wherein I had a points reaching negative 2.8 septillion. It was fun, but there's nothing else to do or worth doing. The other issue is that even when applying fundamentally "correct" strategies, you often—and I mean [b]often[/b]—lose the run quite early on. It makes the choices one makes feel fruitless. The amount of luck that is legitimately required to have a run that goes the distance is way too high, for me. That's coming from someone who primarily plays roguelikes, roguelites, card games, and dice games. The lack of player agency is a bit absurd. It leads to a frustrating experience, and pushes the player towards a perfectionist play-style, which I don't think is very engaging. The game doesn't offer expression or creativity. Pigeon-holes players into a singular winning strategy. One last critique is that you cannot hold down the button to roll your die. This leads to moments when you're mashing the spacebar ad nauseum, because you're trying to roll until you hit a certain point total and have nothing else to do until you get there. It feels monotonous and uninspired. To end on a high note, the sound design and aesthetics are pretty awesome. Overall, it's fun to beat game the first two or three times, but for the price, I cannot recommend. I would recommend buying when the price is $3.99 USD, or less. There are better titles out there that will actually engage your brain and offer 10 - 100 times more hours of enjoyment for this price point.

1. RNG is annoying in this game. Especially with the trials. 2. Trials seem half-designed. Star progression means absolutely nothing when it gives you cards you unlock later. THE ENTIRE POINT OF PROGRESSION TO GET THING YOU CAN ACTIVELY UNLOCK WITHOUT HAVING TO UNLOCK OTHER THINGS. Not wait while doing other things. (For more context, it gives you cards that you can't currently unlock, forcing you to unlock other cards first. Poor design choice.) 3. The "guide" or "solutions(s)" for the trials they claim to have in their discord is 1. NOT IN CHRONOLOGICAL ORDER, and 2. Does NOT have ALL the solutions/guides in it, making it almost ENTIRELY POINTLESS to even join. All in all, this needs some more work, and the devs need to make an actual guide instead of putting low effort into a discord channel. 2/10, deducted 6 for the devs poor design choices, and low effort "guides". Will update IF the above gets fixed. Edit: Reolling locations is an absolute poor design. There's only 4-6 different locations it gives you upon rerolling. I tested this 20+ times, and never got any other locations in the reroll other than those same 4-6. Ever. edit 2: Trials are... not balanced. Having to get 1,500 length of energy circut is just so damn annoying and NOT. FUN. You either sit there and abuse the pyramid's 'impossible face' for discount potions and be bored out of your mind, or be bored out of your mind doing it under 25,000 tiles. Boring, not fun, not engage, bad design. Players should not be forced through a slog fest like this. ANd I doubt the other ones after this will be much better. And, yes, that is the "solution" in their discord. "Sit there and reroll the shop while using an autoclicker to roll your dice" Terrible design. Be. Better. On top of that, most of the other trials are either an RNG fest, or mid difficulty. It's honestly more annoying and tedious than fun. I don't recommend, and I'm sitting at a solid 0 for this game. Not even a 1/10. A 0. For what it's worth, you're better off getting cookie clicker and not dealing with this rng slog packaged as a "fun dice game", which is only fun to people who like to be bored out of their mind, and who enjoy tedious, boring tasks. Hard pass. Would refund if I still could.

At first, the game seemed not worth it. I don't know why they made the standard mode then another one before giving you the game. But overall you need to beat standard mode before the game becomes interesting. I would just drop the player in trial mode immediately to make sure they see the actual game and don't refund after failing the first mode a couple time and not seeing the point of it. The game is trial mode, where your goal is to unlock new cards (passive powers) by completing certain objectives. It's satisfying to figure out the way to get these objective, and then unlocking a new passive which will allow you to complete another objective which you could not complete before. The crucial point of this game is RNG. There is no secret techniques, most little optimization are pretty obvious. And even when you make a mistake, it probably doesn't matter because your not 5 or 10 roll close to success most of the time. THEREFORE This is not a very empowering game. It's possible to play perfectly and fail, it's possible to play suboptimaly and win. When you feel like unlocking a card is impossible (don't pass 10 tiles and score a 32) it's because it is impossible right now with the cards you have. don't be hard on yourself and just do another one. Your chance of success are quite obvious, and the answer is black or white. You will know you've won or failed way before the end. This is not balatro or slay the spire. But it IS relaxing and and i must admit that i get my dopamine rush when i have a good run and when i finally complete an objective using a unique gamestyle the game makes me explore for the time of a small run. If you're looking for a chill, relaxing and decently satifying game to spend time trying to get all the trophies and just going throught the progression, this is a good game. If you're looking for huge big brain roguelike with complicated builds and where you can complete all the challenges as soon as you unlock them if your good enought and have a big brain, this is not a game for you.
